title: Smooth Hermitian Dolbeault forms, metric pairing and operators
statement: Use the usual real and complex fields $\mathbf R$ and $\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $n\geq0$ and let $M$ be a complex manifold without boundary modeled on $E=\mathbf C^n$. A complex differential form is represented by its real alternating covariant tensors in the holomorphic chart chosen at each point. Its coefficients in any other holomorphic chart $e$ are obtained by pullback under the derivative of the coordinate transition from $e$ to the chosen chart at the base point. Let $A^\bullet(M)$ be the complex span of those fields whose coefficients in every holomorphic chart are real $C^\infty$ functions. For integers $p,q$, define $A^{p,q}(M)=0$ when either index lies outside $[0,n]$; otherwise define it as the complex span of the fields supported in exterior degree $k=p+q$ which satisfy $\sum_{j=1}^k\alpha(v_1,\ldots,Jv_j,\ldots,v_k)=i(p-q)\alpha(v_1,\ldots,v_k)$, where $Jv=iv$. These generating sets are complex vector spaces, so their spans are precisely the indicated spaces of smooth forms. A smooth Hermitian metric is a positive definite Hermitian matrix in each chosen tangent frame, with real-smooth transformed matrix coefficients in every holomorphic chart. Its real metric is $g=\operatorname{Re}h$. A metric volume measure is a Borel measure whose restriction to any chart, pushed into $E$, has density $\sqrt{\det G_e}$ against real Lebesgue measure, where $G_e$ is the Gram matrix of $g$ in the coordinate real basis. On $k$-forms its induced pointwise Hermitian pairing is $\frac1{k!}\sum_{a,b}\overline{\alpha(e_{a_1},\ldots,e_{a_k})}\,\beta(e_{b_1},\ldots,e_{b_k})\prod_{j=1}^k(G^{-1})_{a_jb_j}$. Define the $L^2$ pairing by integrating these pointwise pairings and summing exterior degrees $0$ through $2n$. A Dolbeault operator presentation consists of complex-linear maps $D,\partial,D^*:A^\bullet(M)\to A^\bullet(M)$, of bidegrees $(0,1),(1,0),(0,-1)$ respectively, such that $D+\partial$ is the ordinary coordinate exterior derivative, $D^2=0$, and $\langle D\alpha,\beta\rangle_{L^2}=\langle\alpha,D^*\beta\rangle_{L^2}$ for all smooth forms. Thus the differential and its adjoint are fixed by their canonical characterizations, not arbitrary maps. Put $\Delta_D=DD^*+D^*D$, $H^{p,q}=A^{p,q}\cap\ker\Delta_D$, $B^{p,q}=D(A^{p,q-1})$ and $C^{p,q}=D^*(A^{p,q+1})$, with actual smooth images and no closures.
